# has duration

- **CURIE:** [`gmeow:hasDuration`](gmeow-hasDuration.md)
- **IRI:** <https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/hasDuration>
- **Category:** property
- **Defined by:** [`gmeow:slices/events`](../../slices/events.md)
- **Box roles:** [RBox role](../boxes/rbox.md) ([What is this?](../../four-boxes/index.md))

Relates an event to its duration (a [`gmeow:Duration`](../classes/gmeow-Duration.md)). Distinct from [`gmeow:eventInterval`](gmeow-eventInterval.md) (which anchors the event in time); a duration is a length only.

## Structure

**Property shape:** object property; [`gmeow:Event`](../classes/gmeow-Event.md) -> [`gmeow:Duration`](../classes/gmeow-Duration.md)

## Practical Pattern

Use [`gmeow:hasDuration`](gmeow-hasDuration.md) from [`gmeow:Event`](../classes/gmeow-Event.md) to [`gmeow:Duration`](../classes/gmeow-Duration.md) when the relationship itself belongs in the native GMEOW graph.

## Usage Advice

### Use when

- Use to give an event its LENGTH as a quantity — a film's running time, a meeting's planned duration — when only the length, not the anchoring, matters.

### Avoid when

- Avoid it when the event's placement in time is what you mean (use [`gmeow:eventInterval`](gmeow-eventInterval.md) or [`gmeow:eventTime`](gmeow-eventTime.md)); duration is a length, not an anchor.

### How to use

- Point the [`gmeow:Event`](../classes/gmeow-Event.md) at a [`gmeow:Duration`](../classes/gmeow-Duration.md) via [`gmeow:hasDuration`](gmeow-hasDuration.md); the [`Duration`](../classes/gmeow-Duration.md) carries the [xsd:duration](http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#duration) literal on [`gmeow:durationValue`](gmeow-durationValue.md).

### Examples

- ex:film [`gmeow:hasDuration`](gmeow-hasDuration.md) ex:runtime.
